_comment: CAIOS additions to the dashboard's English strings. Deep-merged over vendor/ai4-dashboard/src/assets/i18n/en.json by scripts/build-dashboard.sh, the same way caios.json is merged over _base.json. Keys here win. _comment keys are stripped on the way in, so notes in this file never reach the browser. Written as a merge rather than a patch because en.json is a 900-line upstream file and a patch against it would break on any string upstream touches.

HOME.EYEBROW: CAIOS — Canadian Artificial Intelligence Operating System
HOME.HEADLINE: Research AI infrastructure,
HOME.DECK: A GPU cluster, a curated catalogue of research models, and a control plane that turns one into the other. Medical and neuroscience groups experiment, deploy and serve models here — from a form in a browser to a terminal on the node.
HOME._comment_inventory: Counts, in order: catalog/keep.txt, catalog/ai4life-models.txt, configs/papi/vllm.yaml, and the three site nodes in ansible/inventory/hosts.ini.

INVENTORY.BIOIMAGE-NOTE: Loaded by identifier. The list opens on connectomics.

Every figure in FACT-* is measured and recorded: serverless in docs/oscar-gui-guide.md and docs/oscar-demo.md, federated in demo/fl/README.md, the language model in docs/presentation-2026-08-26.md. CAPABILITY.TITLE: One cluster, three ways to put a model to work.
CAPABILITY.LEAD: The same nodes, the same account, the same catalogue. What changes between these three is which part of the cluster the work lands on — and, for one of them, whether anything is running at all.

SERVERLESS.NAME: Publish a model as an endpoint that costs nothing while nobody is asking.
SERVERLESS.LEAD: Any model in the catalogue can be deployed as an inference service with an HTTP endpoint and a bearer token. Between requests there is no container, no reserved processor and no reserved memory — nothing is running at all.
SERVERLESS.WHY: Everything else on the platform holds hardware for as long as it exists. This does not, so a group can keep many more models reachable than it could keep running. And because it is an ordinary web API, whatever is built on top of it is ordinary code.
SERVERLESS.FACT-LATENCY: measured response, image already on the node
SERVERLESS.FACT-COLD: the first call only, while the image is pulled

FEDERATED.NAME: Train one model across sites that cannot pool their data.
FEDERATED.LEAD: Each site trains on what it holds and sends back weights. The training data never leaves the machine that owns it, and no site ever sees another site's records.
FEDERATED.WHY: For a multi-site study on identifiable data, this is often the difference between a design that can run and one that cannot. The platform's own demonstration splits a public brain-tumour MRI set by patient across three separate machines, and lands within 1.2 points of pooling everything.
FEDERATED.FACT-SINGLE: the best single site, training alone
FEDERATED.FACT-POOLED: all data pooled centrally — the ceiling
FEDERATED.FACT-ROUNDS: ten training rounds, end to end

LLM.NAME: Run an open-weight language model on a GPU in this cluster.
LLM.LEAD: Choose a model, fill in a short form, and a few minutes later there is a chat window at your own address — with an OpenAI-compatible API on the same deployment.
LLM.WHY: Clinical text cannot be sent to a commercial API. Here it does not leave the cluster, and existing code moves across by changing one base URL: the same client library, pointed somewhere else.
LLM.FACT-MODELS: models offered, each one deployed and tested
LLM.FACT-ENGINE: serving engine, on the node's own GPU
LLM.FACT-TOKEN: per token, measured during a federated run

HOME._comment_diagram: Labels for the cluster schematic. The nodes are the machines in docs/infrastructure.md; nothing here is illustrative.

DIAGRAM.ALT: Schematic of the CAIOS cluster: a researcher outside the boundary, the platform inside it, three site nodes holding data that does not move, a GPU node for language models, a serverless node, and an aggregator for federated training.
DIAGRAM.CAPTION: The cluster as deployed. Lit paths are the ones this capability uses; the rest stays on the diagram, because it is the same cluster either way. The marks inside the site nodes are their data — they are drawn in every state, and they never move.

POSITION.TITLE: Built for research groups that cannot move their data.
POSITION.P1: Serious AI usually asks a research group to choose between control and convenience — a managed service that is easy and holds your data, or a bare machine that holds nothing and is yours to operate. CAIOS is the layer in between: scheduling, identity, storage, certificates and a model catalogue, on hardware the group already has.
POSITION.P2: It is one platform at three depths. A clinician-scientist who never opens a terminal, a research assistant calling an endpoint from a script, and an engineer with a full training loop all work against the same cluster, the same catalogue and the same account.
POSITION.THESIS: Train on data that never leaves the hospital — or the country.
POSITION.THESIS-SOURCE: The constraint the platform is built around

COLOPHON.TITLE: Who builds it, and what it is built on.
COLOPHON.LAB: CAIOS is built and operated by PACS Lab as a medical and neuroscience AI platform. The lab runs the cluster, curates the catalogue and holds the accounts.
COLOPHON.STACK: The platform is built on AI4OS, an open-source stack for research computing. CAIOS adds its own configuration, its own catalogue and this interface on top of it.
COLOPHON.HOST: On Canadian academic research-cloud infrastructure. Nothing a researcher deploys leaves the cluster unless they send it somewhere themselves.

CLOSING.TITLE: Start with the catalogue.
CLOSING.NOTE: Deployments, inference services and training runs are created under your own account. Signing in is in the top bar.
